name: Dagar

related.relation: the house-serpent kept by his hall

facts.text: Dagar is a level-60 morvalt named with 8,000 health; a gruppchef and two morvalt larlings come with him.
Allakhazam calls him a plain melee mob with a lot of health; the Stoneheart quest sends players to kill him wearing the runed cloak of the trolls.
Swedish dagar means days; gruppchef means group leader and larling apprentice.
facts.source: Swedish glossary, to verify the morvalt usage

story:
The morvalt keep no calendars, except Dagar. His name, in the tongue the morvalt borrowed for their titles, means days, and he is the one who counts them. On the morning after the morvalt took Trollheim he scratched a single mark on the wall of the hall he had claimed, and he has scratched one every morning since. The wall is full. The next wall is full. The marks run round the hall three times and up onto the ceiling where he has to stand on a bench to reach.

Some of the marks are longer than the others. Those are the days the crazed shamans of the morvalt say bring the Mother closer: the Mother whom the morvalt dig for on Modernagrav, whose waking, they say, will make Trollheim only the first thing that falls. Dagar does not dig. He is a war-chief, not a priest. But he believes, and he counts, and when the count is finished, he says, he will know.

He keeps a small war-band close: a gruppchef, a group-leader he trusts to hold the line, and two morvalt larlings, apprentices learning the count. He fights plainly, with a great deal of strength and no tricks, and he does not like interruptions. Strangers who come to his hall in the runed cloak of the trolls, as the Stoneheart quest sends them, insult him twice: once by coming, and once by wearing the cloak of the people whose city this was. He takes it as an insult to his count, as if they meant to tell him that the days of the morvalt in Trollheim are numbered too.

The house-serpent Fostra Orm sleeps in the warm water near his hall. He feeds it himself. It is the only creature in Trollheim he does not count as a day.
legend: Dagar is straight melee with a lot of health and a small pack: a gruppchef and two larlings. Pull him to a quiet spot, debuff, and grind; a support-spec bonedancer soloed him in eight minutes once. The Stoneheart quest makes people kill him wearing the troll cloak; don't forget it, or the quest won't count, and sometimes he doesn't spawn because something else holds his spot. Two groups is safe. Don't fight him and Fostra Orm together. His shimmering weapons are popular. He hits hard and steadily, so a single tank with a good healer can hold him; the danger is the gruppchef reaching the healer. Kill the larlings last, they barely matter.

aggro: Another day. Another mark on the wall. You.
The troll cloak? Here? In my hall?

loremasterTopic.text: The morvalt who counts the days: a scratch on his wall for every dawn since Trollheim fell, and a longer one for every dawn the crazed ones say brings the Mother closer.

bookPage: From the notes of Hallveig, the Valkyn guide, on the morvalt. My uncles who were not tamed have no word for tomorrow. They have a word for now, and a word for the time before, and a word for the time of the Mother, which is not tomorrow but something else. Dagar is the only one of them who counts. I asked a captured larling what the count was for. He said that when the marks reach the floor again, the Mother wakes. I asked how many marks were left. He looked at me as if I were very stupid and said: fewer.
